ReferenceFailureCode.description:
Why one URL produced no article text.

`ArticleStatus` says which stage ended it; this says what happened there. A
truncated body is its own member rather than a success with less text,
because a download stopped by its byte limit looks exactly like a short
article once the reason is thrown away.
ReferenceFailureCode.title: ReferenceFailureCode

ReferenceQualityFlag.description:
Why one article is not worth putting in front of a classifier.

Every member here was measured on a real extraction before it was written
down. Two candidates were tried and deleted instead: a global unique-word
ratio, which only ever flagged long essays for being long, and an ending
without a full stop, which called 198 complete articles truncated.
ReferenceQualityFlag.title: ReferenceQualityFlag

changelog.why: The cleaning phase writes the same row shape with its text cleaned, and an article it kept but is unhappy about has to be able to say so. It stays empty on an extraction row: the fetch judges whether a page answered, never whether the prose is worth reading.

changelog.change: Initial shape: the manifest identity, the full sanitized text with its digest and word count, the two timestamps, the two tool versions, and the outcome with its typed reason.
changelog.why: The extraction needs a declared row before it writes one (Guardrail #3). The text is the untruncated sanitized prose rather than the capped `Article.text`, because a classifier reading a 2,500-token excerpt is reading a different article from the one a person opened.

description:
What one manifest identity produced, as one element of `articles.json`.

A failure is a row, not an absence. It carries `text: null` with a typed
reason, so the count of URLs that were tried and the count that worked are
both readable from the file instead of one being inferred from the other.

article_sha256.description: sha256 of `text`. Null where there is no text.
article_sha256.title: Article Sha256

article_words.description: Words in `text`. Null where there is no text.
article_words.title: Article Words

extracted_at.description: When the text was taken. Null where none was.
extracted_at.title: Extracted At

failure_code.description: What happened there. Null on a success, and only then.

failure_detail.description: One sentence a person can act on. Never a page's own words.
failure_detail.title: Failure Detail

fetched_at.description: When the request was made. Null where none was.
fetched_at.title: Fetched At

publisher.description: The frozen outlet key, carried from the manifest row.
publisher.title: Publisher

quality_flags.description: What the cleaning phase found wrong with this article. Empty on an extraction row, because the fetch judges whether a page answered and never whether the prose is worth reading.
quality_flags.title: Quality Flags

sanitizer_version.description: Which sanitizer the text crossed the trust boundary through.
sanitizer_version.title: Sanitizer Version

source_line.description: The input line, carried from the manifest row.
source_line.title: Source Line

status.description: Which stage ended this attempt, in the vocabulary the pipeline uses.

text.description: The full sanitized article prose, paragraph breaks kept. Null on a failure, and never an empty string standing in for one.
text.title: Text

url_key.description: sha256 of the canonical URL, recomputed on read.
url_key.title: Url Key
